Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private VPC deployment — post-call recap & next steps

Thanks for the time earlier, Elena — quick recap and proposed next steps from our call this morning. High-level decisions we captured:

- FinServCo is leaning toward a Private VPC deployment (customer-managed VPC with Redwood Private control plane).
- Two networking options are on the table: AWS PrivateLink (endpoint-centric) or VPC Peering (route-based).
- Pilot scope: staging environment (non-prod) first, then prod rollout if throughput/latency targets are met.

Action items for your team:
1) Confirm which cloud account/region you want us to use for the pilot (AWS account ID and region).
2) Share the network contact for VLAN/IP allowlist configuration (we need a point of contact to coordinate security approvals).
3) Provide your current firewall policy and any outbound proxy requirements (we included a checklist PDF).

I've attached a concise network checklist and a sample VPC peering diagram — Vivek and Grace are on this thread to follow up on technical details. Proposed follow-up: 30m session next week with your infra team to finalize the connectivity approach and list of IPs/ports. Please let me know availability.

Best,

On connectivity preference: our infra team has historically preferred VPC Peering for lower operational overhead, but PrivateLink is interesting because of its security posture. Carlos and IT Ops can weigh in on whether Managed PrivateLink endpoints are feasible for their account.

Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Mar 2026 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private VPC deployment — technical clarifications

Hi Elena / Carlos — thanks for the quick reply and the firewall doc. A few clarifications from the SE side to help your infra team evaluate PrivateLink vs Peering: 

1) Egress vs ingress: Redwood's Private control plane needs to reach your VPC to establish a management/control channel and to route inference traffic. The two patterns we typically recommend: 
   - VPC Peering: bi-directional routing between VPCs; we ask that you accept peering and add route table entries for the subnets used by the Redwood service.
   - PrivateLink: we create interface endpoints in your VPC (ENIs) and you only need to open specific ports to those endpoints (recommended if you want tighter surface area).

2) IP allowlist: for peering we provide the /28 CIDR ranges for the Redwood serving subnets (we will hand over exact prefixes after pilot account confirmation). For PrivateLink we provide the endpoint IPs once created; you can also rely on security group rules.

3) Ports/protocols: primary traffic is HTTPS (443) for control + TLS for token-exchange. We also recommend opening TCP 80 for health checks if your team requires unencrypted health probes in staging.

4) NAT/Proxy: if you sit behind an outbound proxy that modifies TLS, we need a short compatibility check — in some cases customers allow a direct egress path from the Redwood agent to avoid proxy termination issues.

5) Monitoring & logging: if you want flow logs or VPC reachability checks, we'll share CloudWatch/VPC Flow Log sample queries.

Proposed technical agenda for the 30m sync: confirm AWS account/region, decide PrivateLink vs Peering for pilot, agree on list of subnets and expected /28 CIDRs to allowlist, and timeline for endpoint/peering creation.

I've attached a proposed VPC peering diagram and a short checklist that maps to your firewall doc. If Tue 3/16 works, propose 9:00am PT.

Cheers,
Vivek Kulkarni
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai

Attachments: proposed-vpc-peering-diagram.png, redwood-network-checklist.pdf

- Subnet range we can allocate for the Redwood peering: 10.20.240.0/28 (we can open that to your serving subnets once you provide the exact prefixes).
